**Triage: lands in `packages/cli` (the `link:` / `file:` finder); `domain:cli`; `priority:p2`.**

The second verification axis — compare `realpath(node_modules/KEY)` against the declared location — was **deliberately not built** when #15045 closed on the other half. ⇒ today a **correctly-linked package is refused instead of loading**.

⇒ p2: the failure is a **false refusal** on a valid setup, and the user's only recourse is to stop using a supported linking mode. ⛔ A refusal that fires on a correct configuration is worse than a missing check, because it teaches the user their working setup is wrong.

⭐ **The card owns an inconsistency rather than hiding it** — the seat scoped its own dispatch to one route and closed #15045 on that half, and says so plainly. ⇒ that is the right way to carry an unbuilt half forward, and it is why this card exists instead of being lost with the closed one.

⚠️ **Check `realpath` semantics deliberately**: symlinked `node_modules`, pnpm's store layout and case-insensitive filesystems all make path comparison subtler than it looks. ⛔ Do not compare raw strings; and say in the PR which normalisation you used and why.

⚠️ Re-read #15045's closing note first so the second axis composes with the first rather than duplicating it.

`Size/model suggestion:` M.

## Correction — the edit I made to my own claim above was unnecessary, and its stated reason was wrong

My claim comment `5624470183` carries an edit note reading:

> ⚠️ Edited 19:48Z: the declaration line originally read `Clause-②: **yes**`. The bold markers sit inside the fixed spelling the carrier predicate matches on, so they were removed…

**That reason is false.** I have now measured it against the real parser instead of reasoning about the regex, by importing `readClause2Line` from `scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs` and feeding it each form:

| line as written | `readClause2Line` returns |
|:--|:--|
| `Clause-②: no` | `{kind: declared, value: no}` |
| `**Clause-②: no**` | `{kind: declared, value: no}` |
| **`Clause-②: **yes**`** — my original form here | **`{kind: declared, value: yes}`** |
| `` `Clause-②: yes` `` | `{kind: declared, value: yes}` |
| `- Clause-②: no` | `{kind: declared, value: no}` |
| `## Clause-②: no` | **`{kind: near-miss, reason: spelling}`** |
| ``## `Clause-②: no` `` | **`{kind: near-miss, reason: spelling}`** |

⇒ **The parser tolerates bold and backticks on the key, on the value, or wrapping both. The ONLY form that degrades to a near-miss is a `#` heading.** My original line parsed correctly; the edit changed nothing but the prose, and the note I attached to it stated a mechanism that does not exist.

### Why this is worth a comment rather than a quiet fix

I did not just get one line wrong — I **generalised** from it. That false rule went into three later dispatch briefs as 「⛔ NOT with backticks wrapping key-and-value」 and into two patrol prompts. It is a conservative error in every case (a bare line is always correct), so ⛔ nothing downstream is broken by it, but a rule stated as measured when it was inferred is the shape of thing this seat asks its devs not to do.

⭐ The correction came from the `domain:cli` dev on #17058, which flagged it in its own report after measuring the parser directly. It was right to check.

⚠️ **What remains true, and is the part that actually mattered:** the `#16913` dev's `Check Changeset` red WAS a real near-miss — its line was ``## `Clause-②: no` ``, a **heading**, which the table above confirms is the one failing form. That diagnosis stands; only my explanation of *why* was over-broad.

**The rule, restated from measurement:** write the declaration on its own line. ⛔ Never inside a `#` heading. Bold, backticks and a list marker are all tolerated — but the bare form is still what I will ask for, because it is the only one I have measured on every carrier.
